text:
Alex: Heads-up — running the HF->Redwood converter on gpt-chat-x produced weird token + weight mismatches. tokenizers have duplicate specials and the model load fails during quantized import.
Priya: Rough error/log paste?
Alex: Error excerpt:
```
ValueError: num_embeddings mismatch (tokenizer:50257 vs model:50260)
During load: 'embedding.weight' shape (50260, 4096) doesn't match tokenizer vocab
```
Alex: Also saw safetensors loader complaining about shard ordering for the quantized files.
Miguel: Could be special tokens inserted after tokenization or the converter reordering added_special_tokens. Did you check tokenizer.json and config.json from the HF repo vs what the converter produced?
Alex: Yep. tokenizer.json from HF lists added_special_tokens = ["<|system|>", "<|assistant|>", "<|user|>"]. After conversion the tokenizer on disk has duplicates and an extra byte-encoded token sequence — looks like a decode issue.
Jen: converter-bot uploaded the artifact for inspection: s3://redwood-artifacts/conv/1763509876/model-converted.tar.gz
Rui: Two things we've seen before: 1) hub snapshot/download without a pinned revision can pick different LFS/safetensors shard manifests, causing shard index mismatch during parallel fetch. 2) converter has an old mapping that assumes HF keys like `lm_head` — but some community models rename to `embed_out` or keep tied embeddings, leading to num_embeddings mismatches.
Priya: Any quick repro steps?
Miguel: Minimal repro: checkout the HF repo commit + run `hf-2-redwood convert --repo . --out ./out` then `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('./out'); print(len(t))"` vs inspect `out/pytorch_model.safetensors` header shapes.
Alex: I ran that. Tokenizer len=50257, model embedding rows=50260. There are three stray tokens that look like the special token strings but with odd utf-8 bytes at the start.
Priya: Sounds like an encoding/escape bug in the converter when it consumes `tokenizer._decoders` or `added_tokens` arrays.
Miguel: Also the safetensors shards: when we reassembled the quantized shards for the dedicated runner the index order mismatched, producing corrupted reads. Converter v0.9.1 rewrites shard file names but doesn't update the manifest in a couple edge-cases.
Alex: Workaround I used locally: 1) pin the HF revision (git rev-parse HEAD) and run `--revision <sha>` to avoid snapshot pick variance. 2) manually edit the converted tokenizer `special_tokens_map` and `added_tokens.json` to remove duplicates, then re-save `tokenizer.save_pretrained('./out_fixed')`. 3) re-run converter with `--skip-shard-rewrite` so it doesn't rename shards. That got the model to load (non-quantized) for evaluation.
Rui: Good. For quantized flows you'll also need to ensure the safetensors shard order matches the model metadata. Quick check:
```
python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(sorted(safe_open('pytorch_model.safetensors').keys())[:8])"
```
Jen: Filing an internal bug and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hf-to-redwood/pull/482 — patch includes: proper handling of `added_special_tokens` (preserve original unicode, dedupe), pinning snapshot_download revision when not provided, and a shard-manifest rewrite test.
Miguel: Another root-cause: some HF model repos include both a tokenizer.json and a separate `special_tokens_map.json` with slightly different encodings (e.g., escaped vs raw). The converter previously favored tokenizer.json but didn't canonicalize strings. Fix should normalize to python str and run `tokenizer.add_special_tokens()` to ensure tie-ins.
Priya: Any impact on chat templates / system messages?
Alex: Yes — because the chat template builder maps template roles to special tokens by name. If token names got duplicated or byte-mangled, the template generator inserted wrong tokens like `\x00<|system|>`, so eval prompts were malformed, giving big regression on instruction-following tests.
Rui: Short-term: if you see malformed specials, open `out/tokenizer.json` and check `added_tokens` and `special_tokens_map`. If there are weird escapes, run a tiny script to sanitize: `t=Tokenizer.from_pretrained('out'); t.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': [s.encode('utf-8').decode('utf-8') for s in raw_list]}); t.save_pretrained('out-fixed')` — then update model configs to match.
Alex: I'll run the sanitizer, re-eval on our prompt set, and upload results.
Jen: FYI QA found a small perf delta when we used the sanitized tokenizer vs original ~0.7% token-per-second loss (probably due to reordered embeddings) — tracking that in the PR.
Miguel: Thanks for catching this. Long-term: converter should include a reproducible end-to-end integration test using a small HF repo with weird special tokens, a multi-shard safetensors package, and a quantized weights path.
converter-bot: New CI run queued for PR #482 — logs at https://ci.redwood.ai/482/1763509876 :white_check_mark:
Alex: :thumbsup: I'll follow up with a reproducer and add the failing HF model repo link in the PR.
Priya: Thanks — ping here when the fix lands so infra can re-run the dedicated onboarding pipeline. :pray:
